title: Your Rollbacks Expire October 23
caption:
I kept a year of Vercel rollback history and never once opened the setting that controls it.

Pro teams now default to 30-day retention, and deployments older than that start getting deleted October 23 unless you opt out. Vercel's own stated reason: coding agents raised deploy frequency, so stored history turned into a cost line. Either way it meters at $0.10 per GB-month now.

My entire incident plan was "roll back to whatever last worked." That plan just got an expiry date.

How far back do you actually roll back?

slides.headline:
Your Rollbacks
Expire October 23
slides.sub: Vercel starts deleting Pro deployments older than 30 days on October 23. Deleted ones can't be rolled back.

slides.headline:
One Year,
Now 30 Days
slides.sub: Vercel's retention docs still list the Pro production default as 1 year, pre-production as 180 days. New default: 30 days.

slides.title: Agents Caused This
slides.sub: Vercel's reason, verbatim: "Coding agents have accelerated development, increasing deployment frequency and the amount of stored deployment history."

slides.headline:
Opt Out
Before Oct 23
slides.sub: Settings / Security / Deployment Retention Policy. Opting out bills it at $0.10 per GB-month.
